params.name: opts
params.type: { actor: Actor|uuid|id|exact name, replace = false, dryRun = false }
params.doc: actor: the character (a wild-shaped form is stored as its original); replace: take the actor from the user it is pinned to

methods.returns: { ok: true, user, actor, previous, cleared, audit, warning?: NOT_OWNER, dryRun? } | { ok: false, code, reason, restored? }
sideEffects: flags.pentaryn-pins.actor on the User (the root actor id)
with replace: that flag deleted on the user who had the actor
switch on and the player online: pullToScene to the token's scene and level (core Scene#pullUsers; a view of what is drawn draws nothing); not when re-pinning the actor they already have
methods.doc: Pin a character to a player: with the pinning switch on, that player's view follows the character's token, and an online player is pulled to the token's scene and level at once. BAD_ARGS for a GM user or no actor; CONFLICT when the actor is pinned to another user (unless replace). warning NOT_OWNER when the player cannot observe the actor (pinned anyway: their view follows a token they get no vision from). A write that throws (INTERNAL) or that a preUpdateUser hook vetoes (REFUSED) changes no pin: the cleared pins are put back (restored: their user ids).

methods.returns: { ok: true, user, previous, dryRun? } | { ok: false, code, reason }
methods.doc: Clear a player's pin (an unpinned user is ok, previous: null).

methods.returns: [{ user: { id, name, active }, actor: { id, name } | null, tokens: [{ id, scene, level, form }] }]
methods.doc: Every pin: the user, the pinned (root) actor, and its tokens on every scene (form: the token's actor name while wild-shaped or polymorphed).

methods.returns: { token: uuid, actor: uuid, scene: id string, level: id string | null, x, y } | null
methods.nullWhen: the pinning switch is off, the user is a GM (even with a pin flag), the user is unpinned, or the pin has no token or more than one
methods.doc: The token a pinned player's view follows. scene and level are id strings (pentaryn-resume reads it at login).

methods.returns: { [userId]: { token: uuid, actor: uuid, scene: id string, level: id string | null, x, y } }
methods.doc: Every pinned player's pinnedToken in ONE walk over the world's tokens, keyed by user id: {} while the switch is off; a GM, an unpinned user and a pin with no single token are absent. For a caller asking about several users at once.

methods.returns: { enabled, ok, pins, violations: [{ code, level, user, actor, tokens: [{ id, scene, sceneName }], detail }] }
methods.doc: Each pinned actor has exactly one token across all scenes. Codes: GM_USER NO_ACTOR SHARED_ACTOR NO_TOKEN MANY_TOKENS (problems), UNLINKED and NOT_OWNER (the player cannot observe the actor) (warnings). Runs whether or not the switch is on; this is the switch-on audit's API return. Deletes nothing.

params.name: opts
params.type: { x, y, scene?, level?, dryRun = false }
params.doc: x, y: canvas point on the destination; scene: id|uuid (default the token's own); level: the destination level id

methods.returns: the pentaryn-portals teleportToken result (pulled included) + { user, viewFollows, online, warning?: VIEW_UNCHANGED } | { ok: false, code, reason }
sideEffects: through pentaryn-portals teleportToken: the pinned token and its company (summons, pets) moved
switch on and the player online: teleportToken's pull names the player, so a cross-scene move pulls them (pullToScene)
switch on and the player online: a same-scene move pulls them to the token's scene and level (pullToScene; a view of what is drawn draws nothing)
methods.doc: Teleport a player's pinned character, with its summons and pets, to a point (portals teleportToken). BAD_ARGS unpinned, NOT_FOUND no token, AMBIGUOUS several, UNSUPPORTED without pentaryn-portals (teleportToken). With the switch on and the player online, portals pulls them on a cross-scene move (pull: [user]). viewFollows: cross-scene, portals' pulled names the player; same scene, switch on, online and the pull sent; a dryRun, switch on and online. warning VIEW_UNCHANGED: a cross-scene move that did not pull the player while they are online or the switch is off; an offline player with the switch on lands on the token's scene at login (resume).

params.name: ref
params.doc: a user or an actor; an id or name is tried as a user first

methods.returns: { user, actor, root, enabled, token, ok }
methods.doc: Read-only pin state for one user or actor, plain JSON, depth ≤ 4: who it is pinned to, the root actor, the token followed, ok = exactly one token. Options are ignored (the root game.pentaryn.inspect passes kind/sceneId/base to every namespace).
Live smoke checks after a sync: the Scene#_onActivate patch installed, setting readable, portals teleportToken present.

settings.doc: The world switch. On: a pinned player sees the scene their pinned token is on and ignores GM scene activation; moving the token moves the player (core's own pull); the sheet shows 'Pinned to'; the GM gets the right-click canvas menu and a toast when a pinned character has no token or a second one. Off: everything in pins is inert.
